problem: Section 1 says emission rows must sum to 1 (Σo b(i,o)=1), but the example's emissions do not: for tag N, 0.5+0.1=0.6, and for tag V, 0.2+0.6=0.8. A student who checks the stated property against the given numbers will think either the rule or the numbers are wrong.
fix: Add one line to step 1: 'The tag vocabulary is larger than these two words. Only b(N,fish), b(V,fish), b(N,sleep) and b(V,sleep) are needed here, so these listed emissions do not sum to 1.' Keep the numbers as they are; the Viterbi arithmetic is unaffected.

problem: Section 1 defines S as the number of tags ('Let S be the number of tags'), then Worked example 1 writes 'tags S={N,V}', using S for the tag set. The same clash appears in Section 3, where S is the tag count in O(T·S²).
fix: Keep S for the tag set and write the count as |S|, or use a separate name such as K for the number of tags: 'Let K be the number of tags', complexity O(T·K²).

problem: The caption says the dashed edge is not on the winning backtrace, but three solid edges (v1→n2, v1→v2, and the dashed n1→n2) are also off the winning path; only n1→v2 is on it. The solid/dashed coding suggests solid means 'on the winning backtrace', which is false. Also, the dashed edge n1→n2 is exactly the backpointer chosen at node N, so calling it 'not on the winning backtrace' without saying why confuses the reader.
fix: Draw only n1→v2 as the highlighted path edge; make the other three light/dashed. Reword the caption: 'The orange node V is the best end state. The dashed edge into node N is the backpointer of the losing end node, so it is not used in the final traceback.'

problem: 'Memory is O(T·S) with all backpointers, or O(S) scores if only the previous row is kept' can be read as saying Viterbi runs in O(S) memory, but Viterbi must store backpointers for every (t,j) to recover the path.
fix: 'Score memory is O(S) if only the previous row is kept, but backpointers must still be stored for every (t,j), so the full algorithm needs O(T·S) memory.'

problem: Subscripts are dropped in the prose: qt, wt, αt(j), δt−1(i), ψt(j) are written flat, while the formula blocks correctly use <sub>. On a phone this makes the indices hard to follow.
fix: Use the allowed tag everywhere: q<sub>t</sub>, w<sub>t</sub>, α<sub>t</sub>(j), δ<sub>t−1</sub>(i), ψ<sub>t</sub>(j).
